description: Promising Practices for Meaningful Public Involvement in Transportation Decision-Making is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by DOT Federal Highway Administration. For transporation departments, quality planning and project development require meaningful input from the public. Many members of the public are genuinely interested in what is happening in their community, but do not know how they can effectively provide input to influence the outcome of a transportation plan or project. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – General, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather. Assets: Transportation and Mobility. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
